title: Solving Linear Equations (KS3)
subject: Maths
strapline: Finding the unknown by keeping the equation balanced.
facts: An equation says two expressions are equal; solving it means finding the value of the unknown letter.
The golden rule: whatever you do to one side, do to the other — keep it balanced.
Use inverse (opposite) operations to undo what has been done to the unknown: + undoes −, × undoes ÷.
For 3x + 4 = 19: subtract 4 from both sides (3x = 15), then divide both sides by 3 (x = 5).
When the letter is on both sides, collect the letter terms on one side first (e.g. subtract 2x from both sides).
Expand any brackets before collecting terms: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6.
Check your answer by substituting it back into the original equation.

quick_quiz.q: What is the inverse operation of multiplying by 4?

teacher_tips: Use a balance-scale image so "do the same to both sides" is intuitive.
Insist on writing each step — most errors are dropped/mis-signed terms.
Always substitute back to check; it builds independence and catches slips.
